newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austrian shares off slightly, CA preferred rebound.
newsitem.headline: Austrian shares off slightly, CA preferred rebound.

text.p: Austrian shares closed moderately weaker on Friday, the last day of trading in January ATX futures, despite a recovery in Creditanstalt preferred shares after more details emerged of the bank's takeover.

The ATX index of 21 blue chip shares closed 1.77 points, or 0.15 percent, down at 1,166.77 after a volatile session. January ATX futures finished 2.2 points up at 1,169, a few points above market expectations.
Traders said the ATX was at the upper end of a trend channel. "On the upside we have room to 1,170-1,175 points and on the downside to 1,150 points," said one.
Overall 14 ATX shares were lower and seven higher.

Preferred stock in Creditanstalt hit a high of 435 schillings, a rise of 17 schillings, on brisk turnover after Bank Austria said it would offer an exchange as part of a takeover deal. The stock later ran out of steam, ending 1.45 percent up at 424 schillings.
Uncertainty over the share's fate had knocked 15 percent off prices this week. Bank Austria won the state's 70 percent of Creditanstalt voting shares at the weekend.

"There was initial demand but then disappointment set in that there would be no cash offer," a trader said. Only small investors holding Creditanstalt ordinary shares will receive cash from Bank Austria.
Luxiery hosiery maker Wolford was the session's biggest gainer, rising 50 schillings, or 3.78 percent, to 1,398.9 schillings.

Fibre maker Lenzing was the biggest decliner, slumping 38 schillings, or 5.78 percent, to a five-month low of 620 schillings after the firm said it expected its loss in the current year to exceed 1996.
The broad-based Vienna Bourse index fell 0.43 points or 0.1 percent to 435.76. -- Vienna newsroom +431 53112 254
